Name: Scream
Review: Scream was actually the first slasher movie that I had ever watched. It was a weird choice considering the fact that the whole movie was also a Satire making fun of the clichés of the horror/slasher genre, and I went into it without prior knowledge of slashers. Not a lot of whodunit's have great rewatch quality. But Scream does. Watching the movie after knowing the identity of the killer and noticing the little clues and foreshadowing is awesome. It's a great film in terms of being a slasher too. As characters are aware of slasher movies and their clichés, there's a lot of great meta moments (I love meta).

I understood why some of the choices made in it might've irked some people. But in the end, as a fan, it was a great farewell. I had to rewatch the first act of Casino Royale to get over this movie though. 😌

It occasionally reminded me of the crazy ideas that we see in Rick and Morty episodes, and that's a compliment.

A must watch for fans of the original.

Review: Nice, funny, entertaining, feel-good pleasure. I wish if they had expanded it to a 30 Rock-ish workplace comedy than just being a movie. Emma Thompson is brilliant.

Name: Bhoothakaalam
Review: A proper modern horror movie in malayalam was long overdue, and this is it! From the way they create a chilling atmosphere inside a most normal and plain looking middle class house, to the way the psychological turmoil of the characters are portrayed, everything builds up the creepiness and leads to a chilling finale. There are influences from other horror movies, but they are smart, the movie is pretty original and avoids several trappings of the horror genre. Gopi Sundar's score is super effective and both Shane Nigam and Revathy were amazing. A lot of scenes were effectively creepy just by the dialogues, performances, atmosphere and music alone. Rahul Sadasivan and team can be proud.

Name: Hridayam
Review: The number of songs and song montages are inversely proportional to the amount of cringey dialogue.

Name: Akhanda
Review:
I honestly don't care about the logic or the clichés or the shitty dialogues or the overused wind machines and leaf blowers. But the whole temple glorification speech and the way the main character's many murders are justified was just too much for my suspension of disbelief. Some of the dialogues in the movie seem like they were written by those uncles who forward all those whatsapp messages about the science of hinduthva or the positive energy field from temples. Yes, mindless movies and mindless entertainers have their own space, but not this dumb, not this dangerously dumb, it's pretty much on the religious propaganda side of things. 

It's an issue when a murderous main character is justified and glorified so blatantly like in Akhanda, even more dangerous when religion is added into the mix, because he's killing in the name of God, and he IS kinda God in this movie. I don't know why it's so difficult to get these points across. Would this movie be accepted the same way if the main character was Muslim and was murdering people in the name of Allah? 

The star is for S Thaman's music. It was pretty cool.

Name: Shyam Singha Roy
Review: It started out good. You know what would have been interesting to see? A My Cousin Vinny, Jolly LLB, Oh My God ish court room comedy about proving reincarnation in court "logically". But what we got was a stretched out flashback, and a rushed cringey badly written courtroom scene that made me regret my wish for this movie to be a full on courtroom film. After watching a Hindu jizzfest like Akhanda, it was refreshing to see a commercial telugu film with an Athiest protagonist who openly speaks against religion and "tradition". Then they decided to include the line about the Ayodhya verdict and I got confused about the whole thing.

Name: Red Notice
Review: People often mistake me for some elitist "Hollywood fan" who only likes "Hollywood" movies and always shit on Indian movies. Well, thank you Red Notice for reassuring me yet again that shitty movies are shit, regardless of the stars, budget, language or the country!

Name: Nightmare Alley
Review: Del Toro chose monsters in human form this time. His unique aesthetics and the atmosphere the movie has make the drama work so much better. The score was perfect, the cast was great. I haven't seen the older film adaptation of this novel, but this is indeed a great film. It's quite an interesting way to handle a con-man story where elements of horror and moody visual storytelling are used as a part of the narrative. The film was gorgeous to look at.

Name: House of Gucci
Review:
In 2021, Ridley Scott released another film called The Last Duel, which was a story set in France and all the characters were French. But these French characters were played by American and British actors, and the movie was in English. So one of the things I appreciated about The Last Duel was all the characters not attempting to do a French accent. They were speaking English with American or British accents.

Now we take House of Gucci by the same director, where all the main characters are Italian, and they're speaking (or trying to speak) with an Italian accent. Now there's nothing wrong with actors doing an accent that isn't their own. Many great actors have excelled at that. Even Jodie Comer who was the lead in The Last Duel has masterfully juggled multiple accents in the series Killing Eve. But House of Gucci handled the Italian accents so badly at times and I was confused if they were being intentionally cartoonish or if they were playing to Italian stereotypes or if the actual people it's based on actually talked like this. Ridley Scott could've just gone the Last Duel route and let the American actors speak American English.

The movie is pretty dull. The true story behind it sounds way more interesting and sad to read than what we see in this film. This is something that required a treatment that the HBO series Succession has, where the humor and drama are well balanced and whenever tragedy hits, we do feel it deeply. Here, a character like Paolo Gucci, played by Jared Leto, whose story is pretty sad and tragic, seems like a cartoon character, accent and all. Leto's performance was great though, he did his best with the material he got. The great Al Pacino does get a scene to scream his heart out, yay! Lady Gaga was obviously the stand out in the cast. Such an amazing performance, and though her Italian accent too isn't all that perfect, her performance makes up for it. The movie could have been a bit more interesting to watch if the final stretch had more Lady Gaga scenes.

I'd suggest that reading about the Gucci family and this incident is better than watching this film.

Name: Mahaan
Review:
Mahaan is a considerable step up for Karthik Subbaraj after a dud like Jagame Thandhiram. The film was engaging enough for me to overlook the flaws. It's more of a genre film than a mass masala flick. All the characters are grey and the film focuses more on the characters, the philosophical side and the drama than being a formulaic star flick, though there's some confusion in the writing too. 

The action scenes were shot and choreographed great, but I don't understand why they did integrate some over the top action moves occasionally while almost 90% of the action was grounded. Great to see Vikram in a movie that I actually enjoyed after so long. Dhruv and Simha were great too. 

Then there's Santhosh Narayanan doing Santhosh Narayanan things with the music, which I absolutely love.

Name: The King's Man
Review:
I think they were more concerned about making all the historical connections and using all those historical figures and events more than, you know, making a King's Man movie. This film was marketed as the origin story of the Kingsman organisation. Instead what we get is a messy and incoherent historic fan fiction that occasionally has one or two of those cool stylish fight sequences that we saw in the other (and far more superior) Kingsman movies. 

In short, random history shit happens with a few minor callbacks to the Kingsman movies (emphasis on the minor) and then they decide to form the Kingsman organisation at the end. That isn't a good origin story, that's just lazy. This whole "origin" could have been explained with a 5 minute flashback in an actual Kingsman movie. It's that thin. 

Ralph Fiennes deserved more. Kingsman is the kind of franchise where even point-blank headshots are reversible. So do a future movie where Orlando Oxford teams up with the current Kingsman agents in the present day and redeem him please. 

Rasputin and his sequences were cool, I wished if that had more screen time.

Name: Freedom Fight
Review: Mixed bag.

Name: Scream
Review:
This is the first Scream movie that got released after Wes Craven's death and it's the first one not to be directed by him. But as I was watching the movie I couldn't tell the difference, it fit so perfectly with the style Wes Craven set in the first movie. They did justice to almost everything that made the Scream films good when they were really good. There's suspense, great kills, humor and a lot of great meta commentary. This is in the league of the first two movies, which were peak Scream. 

Scream was not just about being a slasher or a whodunit, the Parody elements and meta commentary were very much a part of the experience. This movie is constantly making fun of stuff in present day pop culture, modern horror movies by the likes of the stuff Ari Aster, Robert Eggers or Jordan Peele are mentioned, movies having social commentary are mentioned, modern day fandoms are mentioned. And the whole thing is like self aware about it being a sequelish reboot like the Star Wars sequel Trilogy or the Jurassic World movies. The parts in the movie where it made fun of itself or got meta were the most fun of the experience. 

There's indeed stuff that threw me off, like conveniently empty areas that shouldn't actually be as empty as they should be (Especially that fuckin hospital! Which hospital is empty like that, ever?!). While I liked the third act and how they resolved the entire thing. There's something in the very end that did make me cringe a bit. But as there's going to be future movies, I hope that angle gets addressed. But despite of these tiny issues I had with the movie, I still had such a great time watching it, and I got reminded why I had an extra special love for Scream that I don't have for any other slasher franchise.

Name: Uncharted
Review:
The Uncharted video games took a great deal of inspiration from Indiana Jones. They were aiming for a video game experience that felt like an Indiana Jones movie, and they delivered. The characters were interesting, the writing was great and the games actually gave a shit about all that instead of the plot and characters being filler in between the gameplay.

Though this movie tries to emulate the games and even borrow some set pieces right out of them, it couldn't capture the same magic. The writing is the main reason for that, though structurally the movie is similar to an Uncharted game, there's so much nuance that's lost. In the games, Nathan drake was paired with other non playable characters through most of the gameplay. These gameplay sections had constant banter and small talk between the characters that added so much personality to them. A movie does have limitations in doing small talk and banter the same way though, but still, the characters still felt like a shadow of their video game counterparts, though there were occasional moments where the banter between the characters did have the same effect the games had. 

A proper Uncharted film adaptation would've been on par with the Indiana Jones movies (the good ones), this one isn't that adaptation. Still, there's some cool humor and action that I enjoyed in this movie, Holland and Wahlberg were great though they weren't exactly trying to emulate their video game counterparts, and Chloé looked straight out of the video game.

If this movie does become successful and they go forward with their plans for sequels, I hope they adapt the source material better next time.

Review:
സെക്കന്റ് ഹാഫിലെ ഒരു ഡയലോഗ് കേട്ടപ്പോ വിചാരിച്ചത് പടത്തിൽ അതുവരെ ഉണ്ടായിരുന്നതുപോലെ പഴയ പടങ്ങളിലെ ഡയലോഗ് വെച്ചുള്ള സ്പൂഫ് ആണെന്നാണ്. പെട്ടെന്ന് ഒരു ഫ്ലാഷ്ബാക്ക് വന്നു. പിന്നങ്ങോട്ട് എന്തോ ഹൈ ഗ്രേഡ് സ്പൂഫ് ആയിരുന്നു. അവസാനം എഴുതിക്കാണിച്ചതൊക്കെ കൂടെ ആയപ്പോ സ്പൂഫ് പൂർണമായി. തൃപ്തിയായി. 

In 2020 we had Tik Tok: The Movie starring Mammootty, in 2022 we have Youtube Mashups: The Movie starring Mohanlal. What's next? Instagram stories: The Movie?

Name: The Texas Chain Saw Massacre
Review: This is peak low budget horror. The atmosphere and the creepiness just builds up and reaches its high point at one of the creepiest dinner scenes I've ever seen. With cuts and camera angles and shots meant to make the viewer uncomfortable. There's a surprisingly low amount of gore and onscreen violence, and the horror is all thanks to the music and the filmmaking choices. It's not necessarily a slasher either. It's more like a survival horror film. Though this did become the beginning of a gory slasher franchise, this film itself is a different beast altogether.

Name: Texas Chainsaw Massacre
Review:
This movie is also kinda a "legacy sequel", the kind of movie the new Scream made fun of, and it follows the far more superior Halloween (2018) a bit too closely. This is more like an inferior re-skinned (pun intended) version of Halloween (2018) than a follow up to Tobe Hooper's original horror classic. There are some stuff that I liked, some of the gory moments and setpieces were pretty cool, but they were surrounded by so much unoriginal dumb material. One of the things that drew me to this movie was that the people behind Don't Breath were a part of it. There are a few tense moments that did remind me of don't breath, and there's tense and scary stuff here and there, but they'll be immediately cut short by something dumb happening or characters being unreasonably stupid because movie has to movie. The music, cinematography and special effects were cool too. They just had to put some effort into the writing.

Elsie Fisher deserves to be in better films though. She's such a great actress.

Name: The Godfather
Review: Pros and cons of watching the Godfather's 50th anniversary re-release in Indian cinemas: Cons It's apparently not the new 4k remaster, it's the digital version of the old 1972 print that was censored in India (still looks pretty good though) The censoring. A lot of stuff involving blood or gore are cut from the movie in a very jarring way (this includes many iconic moments). Apollonia's topless scene also received the Indian censor board's scissors. (There are no anti-smoking videos and text though, maybe because this was censored in 72) Pros IT'S THE GODFATHER ON THE BIG SCREEN!!!!!!!!!!!!

Name: Columbus
Review: Beautiful.

Name: Bheeshma Parvam
Review:
The "mass" movie has been bogged down to certain templates and focusing on just delivering "moments" for quite a while. If we look at old malayalam "mass" movies that we know and love, our Spadikams and our New Delhis, these movies actually gave a shit about their story and their characters. For them, the main character being a badass was a part of the story being told, and not the other way around where the entire thing solely depended on just fan service. 

Bheeshma Parvam is not a perfect movie, it does have issues, Amal Neerad does indulge in too much style in places that could've worked better in a more subtle approach. But what I absolutely loved about this movie is that it actually gives a shit. It has a story, it cares about the story, it has several characters and it cares about the characters. It's focused on being a film first with actual characters than being a full on fan service vehicle revolving around a star. It takes inspirations from the right places and this is the best larger than life performance by Mammootty that I've seen in a long time. He's totally in his element and is a joy to watch here. Except for a few, I loved the performances of the majority of the ensemble cast. Loved Sushin Shyam's score too.

Review: It's a detective thriller, it's a crime drama, it's a horror film, it's an action film, it's the evolution of a rage fueled vigilante on the road to becoming a hero! It's a true Batman story!

Name: Pada

Name: Spider-Man: No Way Home
Review: On watching it again from home, in 2D, on a TV screen, I had the advantage of proper brightness because the brightness sucked in 3D when I saw the movie in the cinema hall. The third act action sequences seemed a lot better now that I could actually see more clearly what was going on. The fan in me was still jumping with joy at key moments in the movie. On the second watch, I was able to turn my attention away from the plot holes and writing issues and just focus on the Spideyness of it all. I think I would regularly watch bits from this movie for a long time to come. Waiting for the extended/deleted scenes and bonus content to drop.

Name: Valimai
Review:
Action sequences in south Indian movies have hit a saturation point where the "action" is mostly about random slow mo shots of dudes flying and the main character posing to the camera in slow motion, almost like it's more of a photo shoot than an action scene, a lot of posing. Valimai on the contrary has some great action sequences that are actual actual action sequences and you can tell they made a lot of effort into them (well, there's a few duds too).

But the rest of the movie surrounding these action sequences is so shitty that I actually felt bad. There are sequences that seem like they belong in CS Amudhan's Thamizh Padam 3 than a movie that wants us to take it seriously. Much like Vivegam starring Ajith, which provided a lot of source material for the actual Thamizh Padam 2. The cartoonish dialogues and scenes make for some great unintentional comedy. 

Ajith's hair length and hair color changing from one scene to another is another interesting continuity brilliance in Valimai. Did he request fans to stop calling him Thala so that people won't pay attention to his "Thala" while watching this movie?

Name: The Adam Project
Review:
It was fun and entertaining with likable characters, humor and some heart. Way better than Reynolds' previous Netflix movies (6 Underground and Red Notice). Yes it's not so original and echoes other better time travel films, but still though, it had some heart. It didn't feel like a corporate manufactured product like Red Notice did.

Little Adam was love.

Name: Turning Red
Review:
"Turning Red" at its core has the same theme that Greta Gerwig's Lady Bird had. It's about a daughter and her mother, it's about a teenager's conflict between meeting her mother's expectations and being her own person. It does all this while being a kid-friendly, funny, vibrant and fun animated film that has a big fluffy panda, with even a few anime influences stylistically. 

 It's also technically brilliant as all Pixar films are, has a great background score by Ludwig Göransson and cool songs by Billie Eilish and Finneas O'Connell.

Also check out the director Domee Shi's brilliant animated short "Bao" if you haven't watched it.

Name: Salute
Review:
You need to dial up your suspension of disbelief for this movie, because the more you think about certain stuff, the more dumb they seem. Still though, I kinda liked what they were trying to do, though they didn't quite get it right.

I'll suggest "The Pledge" by Sean Penn starring Jack Nicholson for a better take on something similar.

Name: Lalitham Sundaram
Review: It's an achievement to make a 2 hour movie seem like eternity. Not even Biju Menon and Saiju Kurup could save it.

Name: RRR
Review:
Firstly some nitpicking:

1. Bheem wants to save a little girl from an event with a large group of people. To do this, Bheem sets loose a large group of carnivorous wild animals onto this large group of people, a group which includes a lot of innocent people and also the little girl that he wants to save! His entire plan relied on the sheer dumb luck that neither the girl nor himself didn't get eaten by these animals. That has to be the dumbest rescue plan in the history of rescue plans.

2. Alright, an old temple's Ram statue has a working bow and a quiver with actual working arrows. That's alright it's Rajamouli. Those working arrows never end and the quiver always shows to be having the same amount of arrows throughout the action scene. That's okay, it's Rajamouli, and he already did the same unlimited arrow thing in Baahubali. Just don't compare Rajamouli's arrow gang with Hawkeye again. Hawkeye literally spent an entire episode of his stand-alone show collecting arrows because he ran out of them, after firing them.

3. I kinda forgot that Alia Bhatt was in this movie till she appeared in the End Credits song. She doesn't even play a character, she basically just plays a plot device at a point in the movie where the ending has to happen. 

4. One dimensional and over-the-top British villains are One dimensional and over-the-top. Indian movies set in pre-Independance era have always had this thing of portraying all the white people as over-the-top aliens than actual people. I was actually surprised when last year's Sardhar Uddham handled its British characters as actual characters with some depth than as caricatures who are too over-the-top to be considered as humans. 

5. I see what you did there with all those Ramayana references, Mr. Rajamouli.

6. Humor based on characters not knowing English and scenes like showing foreigners how awesome Indian music and dance is are as antique as the period the movie is set in. There might even be a deleted scene where the British woman enjoys Biriyani with NTR and fam. 


What I liked:

1. The pre-interval setpiece apart from Bheem's stupid as fuck plan was awesome. I actually got chills from certain moments in the movie. The deliberately in-your-face fire and water thing was cool at times too. Keeravani's music is reliably awesome.

2. I liked the performances of the two leads and I liked their characters. They had more personality than Daddy and Junior Baahubali combined, who were just cardboard cutouts. (Yes, I don't like Baahubali). They're indeed larger than life, but they do show emotions, and they do get hurt.

3. I have to mention Keeravani again, the music is awesome.

4. The production values are pretty great. There are instances of tacky CGI, but I felt that it looked a lot better than Baahubali overall.

I actually liked RRR. Well, I liked it more than Baahubali anyway.

Ram with a bow, Ram-Bow, Ram-Bo, Rambo.

Alia Bhatt is in this movie.

Name: I Don't Feel at Home in This World Anymore
Review: Dark humor done right!

Name: Morbius
Review: I just felt sorry for all the people who worked for months to produce something that wishes that it was a theme park ride. It's a rusty old swing set at best.

Name: The Bubble
Review: When I first heard about this movie and saw the team involved, what I had in my mind was something like Tropic Thunder that's set in a pandemic bubble film production. Instead we got a dull and unfunny wannabe Tropic Thunder that's definitely Judd Apatow's weakest film that I've seen. Even Trainwreck felt like a better movie and this is coming from someone who doesn't even like Amy Schumer's comedy.

Name: K.G.F: Chapter 1
Review:
I kinda liked this movie despite its issues when I watched it in the theater. Now on watching it again, I got more focused on the issues and tiresome aspects of KGF than what I liked about it, and reevaluated why I liked it in the first place. The headache inducing editing, the horrible dialogue, misogyny and empty hero worshipping that doesn't know where to put the balance between catering to the fans and telling a story. Still though, the things I liked about KGF still stay intact. I still like the structure, the great buildups, the great music, the way it presents its larger than life protagonist and the world building.

If the second chapter is going to be more of the same, I think it'd be tiresome for me. I'm hoping that there's more of a "story" to tell in Chapter 2, and I hope that Rocky actually gets to face a genuine threat than being a god above everything. And I hope that the editor realises that films can be edited together in a way that doesn't induce nausea.

Name: Archana 31 Not Out
Review:
I started watching it after seeing so many negative reviews and initially I felt that it was an okay movie. It's familiar territory but it's the kind of village comedy movie that I usually enjoy. Then the main conflict in the story got introduced just before the interval and it was all downhill from there. The second half is stretched out for a long time with absolutely nothing happening and there's nothing moving at all. To top it all off finally the film decided to build up to a conclusion that actually made me physically face-palm.

There are occasional fun and quirky moments that show promise, but they're just surrounded by such bad writing and execution. I feel the urge to rewatch Thinkalaazhcha Nishchayam just to get a sense on how something like this could be done properly.

Name: Naradan
Review:
The film started with a lot of promise. Firstly I just digged its look and those gorgeous shots of Kochi. It's one of the few movies where the city looks so atmospheric. The movie starts by showing the pressure journalists face while doing their job and develops like a drama. I'm saying this because after a while this tone just shifts. Then the movie becomes something that's far too serious to be considered Satire and far too over the top to be considered a drama. We have sudden character transformations and tonal shifts and over the top scenes, which would have been perfect if it were an irreverent satire on the media like Adam McKay's Anchorman, but when the movie does want us to take it seriously, it just loses its balance. Everything is undercooked and the characters are all one dimensional.

 Just when I thought the movie wouldn't end with a speech about media ethics, it literally did! If they wanted to poke at Arnab Goswami, the better and more entertaining way would've been to make a proper satire, Anchorman style, and not having Anchorman-ish scenes in something that's trying to be a serious drama.

I really liked the film's music too. A piece of music that I heard really reminded me of the theme music from Netflix's House of Cards, seeing that both that series and this film have protagonists who are actually the villains, would that be a coincidence or not?

Name: Beast
Review:
It was fun when Beast was being intentionally funny Die Hard, but it was not fun when it was being unintentionally funny Viswaroopam + Thuppakki + Top Gun + War & Love.

Extra Rants:

Shotguns don't fire their shells as a single bullet, they fire a scattered shot, get educated in PUBG.

I'd rather watch Jonita Gandhi singing Halamathi Habeebo and genuinely enjoying it than the actual music video of it.

Kingsley and Yogi Babu deserved more screen time and they could've saved this movie like they saved doctor.

Nelson expanded on the stuff that didn't work in Doctor (the serious bits), than the stuff that worked greatly in Doctor (the dark humor and the ensemble cast). Why da?

Vijay was reliably awesome.

Name: K.G.F: Chapter 2
Review: Monsters Inc.

Name: Choose or Die
Review: Some good ideas spoiled by awful writing and execution.

Name: X
Review:
This is a better Texas Chainsaw Massacre follow-up than all the actual Texas Chainsaw Massacre sequels combined. The music, the practical gore, the mood, the sets, the prosthetics, the lighting everything just has that late 70s low budget horror movie feel but with a modern twist. I loved the callbacks to Psycho too. Also, like the original Texas Chainsaw Massacre, here's a slasher that just gets straight to the kills without stretched out scenes of the characters doing stupid stuff.

Also, making a porn slasher not seem like porn while also capturing the "essence" of porn is indeed tricky filmmaking, if I'm making any sense.

Name: Ambulance
Review: Bay is at his best when he's unleashing the Bayhem than trying to tell a story. In a movie where it's just 15 minutes of plot exposition followed by a 2 hour action marathon, the Bayhem is at its Bayest.

Name: CBI 5: The Brain
Review: Not as bad as I thought it would be, but not good either. Not as bad as Nerariyan CBI but bad. It's amazing that a movie with a central character who's supposed to be brilliant could actually be this dumb.

Name: Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness
Review:
Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness is indeed a unique Marvel movie. It has Sam Raimi's style written all over it with his signature jumpscares, camera pans, weirdness among other Raimi usuals. Raimi even incorporates some body horror elements and the movie does push the limits on gore and graphic imagery for a PG-13 film that's also meant for kids. I'm pretty sure there was also a shot that seemed like an exact recreation of one from Raimi's first Spider-Man movie. The writer of this movie Michael Waldron had worked in Rick and Morty, he's also the creator of Marvel's Loki. Doctor Strange in The Multiverse of Madness does have more of a Rick and Morty vibe than Loki, not just because this movie also pairs a teenager and a powerful doctor together in a journey that crosses universes, has portals and has alternate versions of the same person.

The parts of the movie that I didn't like were the parts in which it did try to be a generic superhero movie, which included tired tropes that we've seen for ages. But when it's a horror movie or a weird Rick and Morty-ish adventure, it's so fun to watch and is gorgeous to look at and that made the film a satisfying experience. The film looked great in 3D, it's way better in the 3D side of things than Spider-Man: No Way Home.

I did miss Michael Giacchino's Doctor Strange theme music. Danny Elfman does a great job with the music, especially when the movie switches to horror territory, but still I can't even remember what the theme music for Strange was in this film. An action sequence that involved music was also underwhelming. I think on the overall action department, the first Doctor Strange film fared better with that amazing mirror dimension sequence and the reverse destruction sequence.

Cumberbatch is definitely THE GUY after Robert Downey Jr in the MCU. This is definitely Cumberbatch at his best as this character. Elizabeth Olson is great too, but I felt like she didn't do much more than what she had already done in WandaVision. The way Wanda was presented at certain moments in the movie was great.

If you are planning to watch this movie from the theaters, make sure that you reach there as early as you can. You wouldn't want to miss the Avatar: Way of the Water trailer in glorious 3D. Absolutely gorgeous.

Name: Don
Review:
My dislike for films like Hridayam has lowered quite a bit due to watching this toxic and atrociously shitty movie called Don. A "coming of age" movie like Hridayam is harmless in the sense that it gives a few hours of sappy entertainment and some relatability to its target audience and maybe some unrealistic expectations about college and the life beyond to some teens, and then it just ends. It's just a happy world with understanding parents and nice people.

Now take Don, which is kind of trying to be a "coming of age" movie, but in the worst possible way. The movie has the kind of abusive and toxic parent inciting such high degree of childhood trauma to his son that realistically the son would either be suffering from clinical depression or he'd become the kind of serial murderer that the dudes in Mindhunter interview. The son is absolutely terrified of his father in the film. Even after his son is in his 20s, this asshole forces his son to do things he doesn't want. When this makes his son a rebel in his absence, this absolute scum of a human being beats up his son in public. While this may seem like the plot of a dark psychological drama about abusive fathers, this is actually an "emotional" story about loving one's parents! I mean... How cruel do you have to be to write such shit? To preach that toxic and abusive parents "secretly" do love you and that you should love them unconditionally even if they beat the shit out of you whenever they want? They even show a fucking title card at the end that the audience should love their parents, and the model they've set for it is this dude!

Then there's the toxic dictactor of a teacher, the kind of teacher who'd pressure students into committing suicide, who turns out to be a "good" person who just wants the best of his students. Then there's the entire irony regarding how the main character finds his passion (ie, making films) and makes a masterpiece film that paints his abusive father as an angel.

It's so weird that something that starts of as a 3 Idiots-ish thing and is kinda entertaining quickly morphs into absolute trash. Their apparent "message" from the movie is that kids should love their parents, respect their teachers and work hard towards their passion. But this shit is only successful in giving abusive parents and toxic teachers an example or excuse to justify their torture with.

When films like Hridayam just show us an ideal world with nice people and great supportive parents, they're actually harmless in comparison. Movies like Don that make abusive people seem like angels are the kind of shit that these people should just stop making. The acceptance that such content gets is legitimately scary. 

 Even so called "theme park" superhero movies acknowledge childhood trauma yo!

Name: Eastern Promises
Review:
You rarely find a film that's as "efficient" as Eastern Promises. It follows beats that crime movies have followed before, but it does so in a 100 minute narrative that's so "no-nonsense" that not even a second of it is out of place, every scene is important, every frame is important. This movie can be cited as an example of absolute efficiency in storytelling. Even the famous bath house fight scene is so crisp and to the point in its choreography and cinematography.

Viggo Mortensen has the same powerful presence that De Niro and Pacino had in crime dramas, the dude is a legend.

Name: Thor: Love and Thunder
Review:
Thor: Love and Thunder was surprisingly satisfying. There are writing issues and underdeveloped threads which could've been fleshed out, but on the whole, it worked for me. I liked Thor: Ragnarok but it just fell flat at places where it needed us to take it seriously and worked mostly as a goofy comedy movie, and since there was a lot of goofing the movie held up. I don't think anyone cared about Hela's arc of being the banished daughter or her revenge where she kills all of Thor's warrior gang (which is made fun of in this movie itself).

So on balancing the drama and comedy, Love and Thunder did seem better, though Gorr the God butcher still deserved better writing and Christian Bale had a lot more to offer than this. Better than Hela for sure, but not worthy of Christian Bale. Hemsworth is wonderful as Thor, who uses his sense of humor and goofiness as a shield to hide his emptiness. Natalie Portman finally gets to do something in a Thor movie than being a plot device. Thor and Jane have chemistry here that they never had in the last 2 Thor movies they were in.

But yeah, superhero movies should retire the plot device involving kids and parenthood already. But even The Boys, which is supposed to poke fun of superhero stuff, ended with daddy issues being at the core of it, so yk, it's just something we'd still keep on seeing.

Love and Thunder was funny, charming and occasionally touching for me, and when "Sweet Child O' Mine" kicked in at the end, it felt genuinely wholesome. 

Also, Guns N' Roses is love.

Name: Bullet Train
Review:
Bullet Train is the kind of badass action comedy that absolutely DEMANDS a theater watch. The movie is consistent in its laughs, thrills and irreverent tone. The witty characters and funny dialogue blend right in with the film's over-the-top and loud style, even relatably serious characters/dialogue seem funny because of the situation they're placed in (The movie is pretty Guy Ritchie-ish at times). The well shot and choreographed action set pieces were so entertaining that the occasional instances of weird CGI/blue screen felt forgivable.

The only thing I really found interesting in The Gray Man was how Ryan Gosling's character had this reluctant hero vibe going for him. How he is put into a situation that he didn't really want to be in. But that was whole angle wasn't made that interesting in Gray Man. But here though, Brad Pitt's reluctant protagonist is awesome and so entertaining to watch. He just wants to do the job and go home, and what initially feels like an angle that'd lose steam is developed to give hilarious results. Tangerine and Lemon, the two assassins played by Aaron Taylor Johnson and Brian Tyree Henry are the other hilarious standouts of the cast.

Bullet Train is like David Leitch fusing some of the style of John Wick's action with the over-the-top irreverence that Deadpool had. 

An absolute ride. Don't miss it on the big screen!

Name: Thallumaala
Review:
ഒരാഴ്ച ഗ്യാപ്പിൽ തീയറ്ററിൽ നിന്നും കാണുന്ന രണ്ടാമത്തെ "style over substance" അടിപ്പടമാണ് തല്ലുമാല. ബ്രാഡ് പിറ്റ് അഭിനയിച്ച Bullet Train ആണ് കഴിഞ്ഞ ആഴ്ച കണ്ട അടിപ്പടം. രണ്ടു സിനിമകളും മൊത്തത്തിൽ ആക്ഷനിലും കോമഡിയിലും സ്റ്റൈലിലുമാണ് രസിപ്പിക്കുന്നത്, എഴുത്തിൽ ഡെപ്തും ഡ്രാമയും ഒന്നും പ്രതീക്ഷിക്കണ്ട. Bullet Train ഒരു ട്രൈയ്നും പെട്ടിയും കുറച്ചു ക്രിമിനൽസുമൊക്കെയായി വളരെ simple ആയ ഒരു സ്ട്രക്ച്ചറിൽ പോയപ്പോ തല്ലുമാല കുറേക്കൂടി chaotic ആണ് സ്ട്രക്ച്ചറിൽ.

Edgar Wright, Scott Pilgrim താരതമ്യങ്ങൾ തല്ലുമാലയോടു കണ്ടെങ്കിലും അത്യാവശ്യം "structured" ആയ Wright-ന്റെ സ്റ്റൈലിനോടൊക്കെ നല്ല വ്യത്യാസമുണ്ട് തല്ലുമാലയ്ക്ക് എന്നാണ് തോന്നിയത്. ചില യൂറ്റൂബ് എഡിറ്റുകളിലും മ്യൂസിക്ക് വീഡിയോസിലുമൊക്കെ കണ്ട ഒരു വൈബ് ആണ് എനിക്ക് തോന്നിയത്. ചില sequences ഒക്കെ വേണേൽ ഒരു ബിഗ് ബജറ്റ് മീം എന്ന് വിളിക്കാം. വീഡിയോയുടെ മെയിൻ കണ്ടന്റിന്റെ ഒരു ടീസർ ആദ്യം കാണിച്ചിട്ട് പിന്നെ വീഡിയോയിലേക്ക് കടക്കുന്ന രീതിയും യൂറ്റൂബ്‌ വീഡിയോസിന് ആണല്ലോ (പിന്നെ മിഷൻ ഇമ്പോസിബിൾ പടങ്ങൾക്കും). പടം മൊത്തത്തിൽ ഒരു ടിക് ടോക്, റീൽസ്, യൂറ്റൂബ്‌ കളത്തിൽ ആയതുകൊണ്ട് അതേ സ്റ്റൈൽ കൊണ്ടുവരാൻ നോക്കിയതുപോലെയാണ് തോന്നിയത്. അത് ഒരു സോങ് സീക്വൻസിലൊഴികെ അത്യാവശ്യം രസകരമായി വർക്കാവുന്നുമുണ്ട്. പ്രസ്തുത സോങ് സീക്വൻസിനെപ്പറ്റി ഞാനായിട്ട് കൂടുതൽ പറയുന്നില്ല. 

രണ്ടു വലിയ ആക്ഷൻ സെറ്റ്പീസുകൾ ആണ് സിനിമയിൽ ഉള്ളത്. രണ്ടും ഗംഭീരമായിട്ടാണ് അവതരിപ്പിച്ചിരിക്കുന്നത്. സിനിമയിലെ എല്ലാ ഡിപ്പാർട്ട്‌മെന്റ്സും അഭിനേതാക്കളും സ്റ്റണ്ട് ടീമും ഒരുമിച്ചു ആക്ഷൻ മികച്ചതാക്കിയിട്ടുണ്ട്. ഓരോ ഇടിയുടെയും weight തോന്നുമെന്ന്‌ മാത്രമല്ല, അതിലെ "വയലൻസ്" എടുത്തു കാണിച്ച രീതിയും ഇഷ്ടപ്പെട്ടു. ഒരു ഹൈപ്പർ സ്റ്റൈലൈസ്ഡ് സെറ്റപ്പിൽ തന്നെ നല്ല "പഞ്ച്" ഉള്ള ആക്ഷനാണ്. വെറുതേ കൂട്ടത്തല്ലു കാണിക്കാതെ നല്ല structured ആയ, സ്റ്റൈലിഷ് ആയ, കൃത്യം beats ഉള്ള അടിപൊളി ഇടി. "തല്ലുമാല at its best" എന്ന് തോന്നിയത് ഈ ആക്ഷൻ സീക്വൻസുകളിൽ ആണ്. ഖാലിദ് റഹ്മാൻ ഇനിയും ആക്ഷൻ പടം എടുത്തു കാണണം എന്ന് നല്ല ആഗ്രഹമുണ്ട്.

സിനിമയിൽ അടിയ്ക്ക് തന്നെയാണ് ഏറ്റവും പ്രാധാന്യം (if it wasn't obvious already). അടികൾ തമ്മിൽ ബന്ധിപ്പിക്കുക എന്നതിന് പുറത്തു പ്രത്യേകിച്ച് ഗുണം ഇല്ലാത്ത, എഴുത്തിലും ക്വാളിറ്റി ഇല്ലാത്ത റൊമാൻസ് ട്രാക്കിൽ ആണ് "തല്ലുമാല at its worst" എന്ന് തോന്നിയതും. നോൺ ലീനിയർ നറേറ്റിവ് ഒന്നും കുഴപ്പം ഇല്ലേലും ചില കാര്യങ്ങളിൽ കുറച്ചു ലീനിയർ ആയിരുന്നെങ്കിൽ കൂടുതൽ നന്നായേനെ എന്ന് തോന്നി. 

എന്തായാലും തീയറ്ററിൽ നിന്ന് തന്നെ കാണേണ്ട സിനിമയാണ്. ആക്ഷൻ സീക്വൻസുകളും കുറേ സ്റ്റൈലിഷ് ഭാഗങ്ങളും അത് ഡിമാന്റ് ചെയ്യുന്നുണ്ട്. തീയറ്ററിൽ നല്ല മലയാളം ആക്ഷൻ പടങ്ങൾ വരുന്നില്ല എന്ന് പരാതി ഉള്ളവർ ഉറപ്പായും ഈ സിനിമ കാണണം. 

(That final "Reji" from Shine Tom literally made the theater a pooraparamb)

Name: Once Upon a Time... in Hollywood
Review: Netflix India weirdly has a censored version of the movie with lots of muted dialogue, cuts, blurred stuff, smoking warnings and drug usage warnings. Even Quentin's fictional "Red Apple Cigarettes" is muted, because apparently fictional cigarettes cause cancer too. Still though, I just love this movie and rewatching it is always a joy. Next time I'd totally avoid the Netflix version though. Quentin would probably flip out at them if he saw what they did to his movie.

Name: Day Shift
Review: Yet another Netflix movie that just screams "generic". Everything from the buddy cop setting to the vampire stuff to the action are mere shadows of things that superior movies have done before. There are occasionally cool moments of action, Jamie Foxx or Snoop Dog, but overall I'd rather rewatch the Fright Night remake or the Wesley Snipes Blade movies.

Name: Elvis
Review:
Baz Luhrmann's Elvis does tread through the familiar "rise of a music legend" template for about half of its runtime. There are stylistic choices from Luhrmann that makes it unique, Elvis himself gets the kind of  introduction sequence that a larger than life hero gets in movies with a huge buildup and anticipation as he makes his way to the stage to deliver the performance where he's discovered first. There are multiple montage sequences which are slickly edited with a lot of stylistic flair. What makes Elvis' story unique is the relationship he had with his manager Colonel Tom Parker. The movie begins through Parker's perspective, it lets us see Elvis through Parker's eyes, as a powerhouse of sheer talent and an opportunity. As Parker helps Elvis in his journey to greatness, it's evidently made clear that Parker's intentions are not so pure.

Tom Hanks is playing against his "nice guy" type here as the grey and manipulative Colonel Parker, though his inconsistent accent, occasionally over-the-top performance and prosthetic makeup made me feel confused if those choices were intentional or not.

 But without any doubt, this is Austin Butler's movie. Austin Butler's performance as Elvis through various stages of his life is powerful. Through the stage performances and quieter moments he just carried the movie with such energy. You'd expect a film that has Tom Hanks and a newer actor to have some kind of dominance from the more senior actor, but Butler just steals every scene he's in. Even at places where the writing is pretty surface level, Austin Butler rises up to elevate those moments. The third act of this movie alone is just enough to get him all the acting awards this season. The third act is where Elvis becomes a bit of a character driven drama too, with the Colonel's manipulation and Elvis' struggles taking the stage.

At the final scene of the movie, the scene shifts from Austin Butler to archive footage of the real Elvis and that transition looked so seemless! That's how fucking good this dude was!

The soundtrack also has some beautiful renditions of Elvis' music.

Name: The Firm
Review: "They don't run me and you don't run me!" - Tom Cruise who gets to run like Tom Cruise in a lawyer movie.

Name: Vengeance
Review:
A different kind of murder mystery/revenge movie that shakes up the already set template for such stories. Written and Directed by The Office's BJ Novak, Novak himself stars in the film. It's about a journalist who puts himself in the middle of the death of a girl he has casually hooked up with. Her family thinks that he's her boyfriend, her brother thinks it's a murder and wants revenge. The main character Ben sees an opportunity to use this story to do a podcast.

The movie starts off by introducing the protagonist who's basically a self centered pretentious a-hole, and then when he travels to Texas to meet the girl's family, there's a lot of situational humor that did remind me of the kind of humor from The Office. Then the movie becomes surprisingly deep and drama elements come in. Even some of the pretentious sounding dialogue attains meaning as the movie moved forward. The characters are great and there's some great dialogue. The music by Finneas O' Connel was also beautiful.

The Dark humor and murder mystery aspects do lack a certain "punch". While Vengeance doesn't reach the levels of something like a Coen Brothers movie, it's still a great watch. I've always wanted to see a revenge story where the protagonist is an asshole who doesn't even care about the person who died.

Name: The Hunger Games
Review: The world building is great, the buildup to the hunger games is great, the character work is great, the score is great, the mood is great. But whenever the movie switches to action, it's just incoherent shaky cam, weird angles and rapid editing that just insists that we don't clearly see what the fuck is going on. But luckily those kind of action sequences don't spoil the enjoyment of the film too much. Jennifer Lawrence is love.

Name: The Hunger Games: Catching Fire
Review: Everything is better than the first movie. The action is shot better, the movie looks better, the stakes are bigger, the world seems bigger and the villains seem more dangerous and of course, Philip Seymour Hoffman is in it. That aspect ratio transition when the game begins though *Chef's Kiss*

Name: The Hunger Games: Mockingjay – Part 1
Review: It's entirely buildup towards the next film so it's a lot different from the last two installments. It plays out like a drama, it's not as vibrant as the last movie, and there's a sad and grim tone throughout. Of course I didn't like it as much as the previous movies. But I'm treating this as a buildup episode than as a stand-alone movie and I'm immediately watching part 2 after this (which is a choice that people who saw this in the cinemas clearly didn't have).

Name: The Hunger Games: Mockingjay – Part 2
Review:
It's pretty satisfying as a final installment, they did add plenty of drama and conflicts and kept it away from some of the usual predictability territories. Not as action heavy as I expected it to be, but I'm not complaining. It also made me miss Philip Seymour Hoffman a lot.

I can say this though, Catching Fire is the best Hunger Games movie. Period.

Name: Orphan: First Kill
Review:
The first Orphan movie is remembered for two things, the terrific performance by the then child actor Isabelle Fuhrman and the big twist at the end. This prequel does get so many things right as a companion to that film. Firstly we have the adult Isabelle Furhrman reprising her character, which brings a whole new interesting angle to the movie and her performance is amazing in this movie too. The Lord of the Rings style height illusion techniques too are pretty effective and impressive in a lot of sequences. Although I could spot when the child double actors where used at times (then again, I've spotted the hobbit doubles in LOTR too, I just look for this stuff too much I guess).

Don't expect a big twist like the original movie had. Still though, I liked the way they still did something fun and interesting with the prequel than being just a rehash. Julia Styles was great too

Name: Glorious
Review: It started really strong but then it lost steam and felt dragged out. A 75 minute long movie feeling really long is not that great. Good performances though.

Name: DC League of Super-Pets
Review:
This is a movie that I've seen so many times. There's the Buzz and Woody dynamic between Krypto and Ace, there's the use of pop songs, there's the talking animals but the talking seems like them making animal sounds to humans joke being used over and over again, there's the obvious setup to the ending and there's beats being followed that a lot of animated movies have followed before. I won't say the turtle time freeze thing is a Quicksilver scene rip-off, because an animated movie called Over the Hedge did that stuff way before X-Men did with the squirrel voiced by Steve Carell.

Basically there's not a lot that's original about this movie except for how it uses already established DC characters and the art and animation style. Keanu Reeves' Batman deserves his own Spin-off. I did have a lot of fun watching this movie and it did make me smile.

Name: Nope
Review: I watched this movie having no idea what it's about because I used both Peele's previous films like that and I'm so glad I did that. This is a proper effective horror movie and the stuff it does with the subgenre it's playing with is great! A lot of standout sequences, great design, great music, great visual effects and amazing cinematography.

Name: Ad Astra
Review:
There are some gorgeous visuals, great action setpieces and a great near future setting. But at times it was hard to care about the monotonous and perpetually sad protagonist and his dad (which is a relationship that the movie doesn't develop much though the entire movie is based on it).

Is the title a typo though? Because I'd have called it Sad Astra. As in Sad Astronaut. Hehe.

Name: Psycho
Review: I can't believe how thrilling it was even after years of pop culture spoiling the entire plot to me.

Name: Paappan
Review: Hats off to Joshiy for being the one aspect of this movie that didn't feel ancient.

Name: Brahmāstra Part One: Shiva
Review:
While watching Brahmastra Part One, I could indeed feel the care, love and passion that Ayan Mukherji had for it. As a kid who grew up reading Amar Chitra Kadha and watching anime, superhero cartoons, movies and franchises like Harry Potter and Star Wars, the kid in me also wanted to see something like Brahmastra. So this movie essentially is like a kid's fantasy coming alive, a world that has that kind of wonder being a part of it. Ayan tries to integrate this imagination into a generic 90s and 2000s bollywood movie template, which might also be what the kid in him wanted. But as a result, we get something that also has several clichés, melodrama and dated writing that it could've easily avoided to become a better movie. While developing his world, mythos and the look of the film, Ayan gave little importance to the basics, and it does hurt the movie.

The romantic arc between Shiva and Isha is supposed to be the soul of the film. It's something that the whole movie spends a considerable amount of time on. But even then, despite it being Ranbir Kapoor and Alia Bhatt together on screen, it falls flat. It's barely developed and the characters just zoom past to the point of true love where while it's being said on screen how strong their love is, we just never feel it. Though with beautiful tracks like Kesariya playing in the background and Ayan being the person who wrote Wake Up Sid, I didn't expect the romance to be the most underdeveloped aspect of Brahmastra.

There's also the issue of underdeveloped supporting characters. Too much time is taken on exposition and world building that occasionally the movie forgets to tell its own story (that's one flaw of the MCU that an Indian movie also has now, hehe).

Despite the flaws, I still enjoyed Brahmastra. Like I said above, I could feel the passion and love that Ayan Mukherji had for this world. There's a certain amount of genuine imagination in Brahmastra that I rarely see in hyped up big budget Indian movies. The action sequences were all well designed for the most part. The decision to depict the powers using bright and vibrant colors was spot on, and the movie genuinely looked gorgeous when the Astra powers were on display. Though I had mixed feelings about the visual effects after watching the first trailer, while watching the movie itself, I indeed bought into it and it looked great (except for the very last portion of the movie with the orange filter). Simon Franglen's score and Pritam's songs were great and tries to do a lot of heavy lifting for the terribly written romance arc.

I do want Brahmastra to succeed though, Ayan's world does show promise, and with a lot of exposition thrown into this movie, maybe he can focus more on the characters and the story in the next movies. There's a lot of interesting stuff worth exploring here and it's a much better franchise material than other successful Indian multi-part films which were nothing more than re-skinned versions of stuff we've been seeing for years. I'm not saying that Brahmastra is completely devoid of generic material, but it also has sparks of originality and imagination that I'd really like to see more of.

Name: Sita Ramam
Review:
Sita Ramam started off like a bland military movie that didn't capture my interest. Then it switched to the present day frame story with Rashmika Mandanna's monotonous character and it didn't feel interesting either. Enter the title characters, then the movie transforms into a pretty nice love story with great locations, beautiful sets, great cinematography, beautiful music and great looking costumes (The people who did makeup, hair styling and costumes for Mrunal Thakur in this movie deserves awards). So the best part of Sita Ramam was indeed Sita and Ram and how their story develops into something heartfelt. Otherwise the handling of Indo-Pak conflicts and the religious conflicts were pretty juvenile, Ram was occasionally too virtuous to an annoying degree, though he was likable. Sita was love throughout.

I haven't seen Veer Zara, so I don't know what to say about that whole comparison. The movie could have benefitted from a lesser runtime and more focus on Sita and Ram than on the army stuff.

Name: The Assistant
Review: Perfectly paced and brilliantly written and acted. The movie begins as we see the main character going through a mundane work day with usual work stuff she has to deal with as an assistant. Meanwhile there's indeed stuff happening in the background while she's working. Slowly it becomes clear and then the movie becomes this powerful and sad work of art. The pacing is still the same, we're still going through her work day, but it gets darker. There's also a hint of realism and a not at all glossy style that works wonders for the movie. The short runtime is also effectively used. Julia Garner carries the movie brilliantly.

Name: Beast
Review: It's pretty generic but I loved the action, the way the animal scenes are shot like the bear attack scene from the revenant and the great CG lion and how it's depicted and shown as an absolute beast.

Name: Attention Please
Review: I liked some of the things they were trying to do and disagree with some others. But the movie could've benefitted from being 30 minutes or so shorter.

Name: Vendhu Thanindhathu Kaadu
Review:
There's a lot to appreciate in VTK, Muthu's journey from an insignificant helper boy to a gangster has many great moments. There are brilliantly designed action sequences, a terrific background score and soundtrack from A R Rahman and a really specific look and style that really captures the atmosphere the story is set in. The use of long takes in several important scenes also seemed to serve a purpose and convey the drama and tension of those moments than being a gimmick. Silambarasan is brilliant and the subtle touches he brings to Muthu really sells the fact that this is the same person though the transformation that occurs to him is very big. 

Muthu is treated as a character here and not as a hero or a "star", so there's no hero worshipping, no punch dialogues, no heroic slow-mo, nobody is praising how great he is and so it's also pretty easy to accept his flaws as he's pretty human. So for all intends and purposes, this is a pretty grounded gangster story. Though some of the gangster story beats are familiar, there's a certain amount of nuance, world building and atmosphere that gives it an identity of its own. I'm not saying that the writing and world building is perfect, there are flaws, but it was still interesting enough for me to forgive the flaws.

After Brahmastra, this is the second week in a row that I've been disappointed by the romance arc done by an Actor - Director combo that made one of my favorite love stories. I saw in an interview that the reason for GVM having a shared writing credit for the script is that the writer Jeyamohan made GVM tweak the script especially for the romantic arc since that's not Jeyamohan's forte. The romance arc is indeed the part where the movie's balance falters. Though it's backed by great music from Rahman's side and nicely shot song sequences that reminded me of "Anbil Avan" from Vinnaithandi Varuvaaya, the way it builds up is, you know, weird, to say the least. I don't know if naming the one dimensional love interest "Paavai" and making her utter lines that specifically point out the weirdness of Muthu's approach was some kind of self parody writing. Though the love angle is not throwaway and is indeed an important part of where Muthu eventually ends up, its placement and execution was flawed.

So, weird love angle and forgivable flaws aside, VTK is indeed a gangster story that I really enjoyed. I'm sure that I'd revisit the movie after it's out for streaming and I already have the soundtrack on loop. Those well-shot, well-edited and well choreographed action sequences with no slo-mo gimmicks itself makes it one of my favorite movies.

I did see people comparing VTK with KGF. There are some surface level similarities like the Mumbai gangster angle and the long beard look at the end. But this movie is doing something entirely different, and if we were to compare the two even then, Rocky Bhai with his self praising catchphrases and endless metaphor dialogues would seem like a cartoon character in comparison.

Name: Three Thousand Years of Longing
Review: I did not start watching this movie expecting something this wholesome. The music and visuals were beautiful, Elba was great and I loved the whole style of the movie.

Name: Confess, Fletch
Review: This was a really fun movie that starts off as a generic mystery comedy and then brings in a lot of fun quirky elements that does indeed make it unique.

Name: Do Revenge
Review:
This film was a surprise. I remember seeing it on Netflix and thinking it's one of those cheesy high school romantic comedies that Netflix occasionally puts out, but I was wrong. Do Revenge reminded me of the kind of high school movies from the 80s till early 2000s, before the American Pie - Superbad set of movies came in. Do Revenge is not as dark as Heathers and not as light as Mean Girls, but it's somewhere in that space of things, with a Gen-Z twist of course. 

Though the characters are over-the-top I loved the way how the "Gen-Z ness" was integrated into the movie. It's indeed impressive to make fun of characters being woke, without being insensitive and actually being woke. There's a surprising amount of depth and complexity too. 

Though the ending felt a little "easy", the movie as a whole was still fun. Good watch.

Name: I Used to Be Famous
Review: Wholesome.

Name: Avatar
Review:
In 2009, as a kid, I remember being so disappointed and sad that my parents wouldn't take me to go see Avatar. I pleaded with them but it didn't happen. So, when I got to watch it, it was a CAM rip DVD, playing on an old CRT TV, and it still managed to blow me away. I haven't even kept track of the number of times I've revisited it as a kid. I've even rewatched the extended cut multiple times.

So now, when older and more bitter me got a chance to catch Avatar on the big screen again, it was indeed a new experience, both technically (since it's a 4K 3D, 48FPS version), and emotionally. I was once again blown away by the movie, the visuals, the kid in me really became alive again. But the older me could also notice flaws in the film that the kid me didn't. Some of the dialogue did lose its lusture, there are many plot conveniences and then there's the white savior aspect of it.

But regardless, the movie looked gorgeous in the big screen format. All the things that made me fall in love with it are intact, James Horner's score sounds like a dream through the cinema speakers. 

And finally, when the sequel sneak peak was shown, damn. It looked more majestic than any other CG 3D movie I've seen, I've never seen anything that looks like this on a cinema screen, I mean damnnn!!!! I can't wait to be blown away once again by Mr. Cameron and team in December.

Name: Bodies Bodies Bodies
Review:
Such a unique and smart spin on a familiar template. Awesome dialogues, intelligent writing, brilliant performances, great music, great cinematography, art direction and a great use of darkness to create mood. The characters were intentionally caricaturish and yet there was something real about them too. The burns at elite surface level woke young peeps were also cool.

Pete Davidson made me feel that he was just playing himself at a lot of places though.

Name: Music and Lyrics
Review:
This is one of the movies that I've watched in HBO India multiple times when I was a kid. Even now on the rewatch it just felt so wholesome. It's like comfort food for me. It's the kind of cheesy that I enjoy with a wonderful Hugh Grant and Drew Barrymore carrying the movie, plus great music too.

Kinda motivated me to check out other Hugh Grant romantic comedies during the 90s and early 2000s too.

Name: Begin Again
Review:
The absolute joy of watching people bond over music is the reason why I love this movie. Having a headphone splitter and vibing to the same music together on the city streets is THE dream for me.

And fuck Marvel for preventing us from having more of THIS Mark Ruffalo.

Name: Mistress America
Review:
Mistress America isn't as emotional or deep or personal as Frances Ha, it's on the lighter side of things. But I do think it's the funniest Noah Baumbach movie I've watched, I laughed at multiple points. The humor is mostly through character quirks, detailing and awkward conversations. The movie flows in a pretty breezy way and it reaches the place in the 3rd act where we expect conflict and drama. But the movie surprised me by staging the whole situation as a laugh out loud comedic scene, Greta is so amazing here, even some of her stares made me laugh. Combine that with the brilliant dialogue writing and the editing style that flows with the dialogue, it's a joy to watch. Noah Baumbach's skill at staging arguments and verbal fights is just so unique and brilliant. 

Some of the themes are similar to what we saw in Frances Ha, but this is a different and more comedic movie. There's is a layer of sadness in the movie, but it communicates it mostly through comedy. And I just fell in love with the dialogue ❤️

"Being a beacon of hope for lesser people, is a lonely business"

Name: Ponniyin Selvan: Part I
Review:
The action in PS-1 not ripping off Zack Snyder's 300 itself felt refreshing (as that trend has gone on for more than it should). They were aiming for a grounded and kinetic style similar to what Ridley Scott and team did in Gladiator, but it doesn't really succeed in it (while Scott himself has done it again well in last year's The Last Duel). While the action in PS could've been better, again, I'm glad it's not 300!

PS-1 is less about that kind of spectacle and more about other kinds of spectacle, it tries at least, to have substance. Its priorities lie in its storytelling, its characters, the world it's set in and the drama that's fueled by vengeance, love and the hunger for power. Though I love A R Rahman's soundtrack for the film, some of the song sequences felt like they were halting the narrative than complimenting it. There's a unique atmosphere set by the movie and the performances were also great, especially Karthi and the two scene stealing female leads (Aishwarya Rai Bachchan and Trisha).

I'd have really struggled to understand the old timey Tamil if the cinema screen didn't have English subtitles (Thanks projectionist person!). The movie would have benefitted from having more detailing and world building. Because there are interesting characters whom I wish I got to know more.

Since Mani Rathnam had already finished production on the sequel too, there's no use in saying "I hope the sequel fixes these flaws". PS-1 was pretty satisfying on the whole for me.

Name: Blonde
Review:
I'm confused about this movie. The only thing I can say for certain is that Ana De Armas delivers a brilliant performance and that I really loved the visual style and the music. But the narrative is where my confusion lies.

This is in no way a celebration of Marilyn Monroe as an artist or an icon; it's a fictional take about Norma Jeane, explaining her psychological turmoil and the horrors she had to face, with cherry-picked events from the real Monroe's life only being referenced as it goes along. It's graphic, sad, and has disturbing imagery at times. If we even just read Monroe's Wikipedia page, we'd read about a woman who fought through abuse and condescending men, who, in a time of widespread misogyny, did try to do roles that had meaning and even start her own production company. Though she was mostly typecast as a sex object, she curated her own image and didn't shy away from showcasing her beauty. Norma Jeane in this movie is a sad and disturbed person; she's constantly victimized, and we don't see her as a fighter or a survivor.


Another thing about Monroe is how the media has been sensationalizing her throughout her career and even after her death. There are numerous versions of her life, what happened to her, and what she went through. So is "Blonde" supposed to be a meta-narrative that critiques the movie industry, misogyny, and how the media depicts this woman? There is a deliberate choice to make this more fiction than fact; there are many outlandish sequences that disturbingly depict how men thirst at the sight of Monroe; there's a dream-like quality to the film. So I don't know if the intentions of the film are to show us a version of her that the media was always keen on showing and then show us a disturbed individual going through psychological trauma instead of a glam queen.

So I'm not sure where I stand on this movie. It was not an easy watch for me. I don't know if the narrative choices were deliberate or if the movie is just bad and disrespectful. So I was just confused by blonde.

Name: Thiruchitrambalam
Review: While acknowledging how cheesy and familiar it is, this movie felt so wholesome. I was smiling through most of it and I was connecting with the characters and their emotions. Anirudh's score was great, the performances were great, the songs were placed at perfect places. It left me with a smile on my face. Also, I admire the fact that Dhanush can completely shed his star persona and do something like this. Even at the point where we'd expect a VIP-ish heroic scene and badassery, the movie handles it a lot differently.

Name: 20th Century Women
Review:
The title is a bit misleading. I watched this movie without knowing anything about it and was surprised that it's actually more about a teenage boy than the titular women. We see the 3 women through his eyes mostly though sometimes the movie does switch to their perspective. It's a slice of life kind of movie with very minimal drama and really likable characters and some touching moments. Greta Gerwig is the standout performer for me, and special mention to Billy Crudup for making me laugh in that dinner scene. Annette Benning is also great as the mom, but as she's already delivered something as brilliant as American Beauty, a character like this is a cakewalk for her.

I loved the music and cinematography and the style of the movie too.

Name: Natchathiram Nagargiradhu
Review:
This movie made me feel kinda similar to the way I felt watching "Da 5 Bloods" by Spike Lee. Though Da 5 Bloods at least felt more entertaining. When Ranjith used the boxing movie template to show caste and history, it worked like a charm. Sarpatta Parambarai felt rich and moving, it had something that's so lacking in this movie. This just felt like a political speech or documentary presented as a movie. I didn't care that much about the characters, I rolled my eyes every time the same statements were being repeated even after the point was made. I admire the thought behind the movie, but it just came off as pretentious a lot of the time. A character literally lectures another character about subtlety in the movie itself, but this movie is anything but subtle! The lack of subtlety would've been okay too, if the actual movie around these political lessons was more interesting.

As someone who loves Ranjith's previous movies (even the two Rajini ones), this one felt so disappointing. Loved the music and Dushara's performance though.

Name: Blue Jay
Review:
This was such a beautiful movie. With just two characters mainly and told entirely through dialogue, we just feel like these people have lived this life, and that they've all this suppressed love just by the energy that they have. It's kind of like a sadder version of Before Sunset. While we actually did see the young love blossoming in Before Sunset's predecessor Before Sunrise, in this story of former lovers seeing each other after a long time, the only direct peek we get at the time when they used to be lovers it is through an audio recording, in a brilliant scene that shows us the present day Jim and Angela reacting to their younger selves and then trying to recreate it.

Even at the places where they're just bonding and having fun, there's an inherent sadness, the possibility of "what could have been", and that was just beautiful. The use of music in the movie was also beautiful, Paulson and Duplass were brilliant and the character interactions and dialogues just felt so real. Even more impressive considering it's mostly improvised.

Name: Entergalactic
Review: Beautiful. Just. Beautiful.

Name: Hasan Minhaj: The King's Jester
Review: I do dig "PowerPoint stand-up". It's cool when visual tools like that are also part of such a performance.

Name: Constantine
Review: I loved the atmosphere, the visual effects and the whole style they were going for. Very noir-ish. Keanu was great and I'm glad this is getting a sequel, though pretty late.

Name: The Hustler
Review:
Movies based on a sport or a game tend to give too much importance on the winning or losing. After reading the plot synopsis of The Hustler, I thought it'd be the kind of thing where the protagonist Fast Eddie would lose to Fats first and then work on himself to beat him in a thrilling final match. But what I got in return was a character study, which is occasionally sad, with a flawed protagonist who is unable to see past the hustle till something terrible happens to him. It's about him being ignorant towards what his actual priorities should be.

So when finally the rematch of Fats happened, the film gives little to no significance to it, as in there's no attempt to make it dramatic or thrilling, it's all about the character there. Then it is followed by some amazing delivery by Paul Newman, who just oozes in charm, charisma, anguish and general selfish assholery as Fast Eddie throughout. Then there's the Piper Laurie, brilliantly playing an addict with her own issues, who still feels like the only sane person in the movie's world filled with people who'd spent 25 hours continously just for the sake of hustling or gambling. The romance arc did make me feel "Why doesn't she leave this asshole yet?!", or "How did they end up together anyway?!", but the movie did have answers to these questions for me.

Name: Rorschach
Review:
Rorschach wastes no time to get into its plot. We're put right into it from the first scene itself. It's got the vibe that a lot of those Hollywood and European psychological dramas set in a small town have. It's moody, has dark colors, the characters have a sense of weirdness, and then we have the main character who's the weirdest of them all. It takes a familiar trope and gives a pretty unique spin to it, I don't know if someone will emerge saying that it ripped off some Korean/European/American movie, but for now, I'll just say I liked the way it handled its narrative and the way its structured. The movie uses tricky editing at multiple places effectively too. Extra cheers to editor Kiran Das and the production design team. I also loved how the movie behaved when it got surreal, there's no over-the-top post production effects, it's rather done in a Twin Peaks-ish way. The occasional dashes of dark humor were nice too. I think this is the closest a Malayalam movie has gotten to the general vibe of something like Twin Peaks (The original series, not extreme surreal territory like fire walk with me or the return). The setting and its atmosphere looked really unique. 

Couple that with amazing performances from Mammootty, Bindu Panicker, Jagadish and the rest of the cast and a cool background score, Rorschach was satisfying, though it does lose focus occasionally and the attempts to make the main character more "commercial" with repetitive looking fight scenes and slo-mo at times didn't exactly sync. I liked the way in which main character is presented and written otherwise. It's the kind of Anti-Hero that we don't see that often, especially from a star.

Name: Werewolf by Night
Review: Everything about this was dope. The style, the music, the cinematography, the use of light, the special effects, the costumes, the performances, all capture the classic monster movie vibes perfectly, and the few minutes that the titular werewolf appears on screen was awesome.

Name: Hellraiser
Review: It's a low budget horror movie from the 80s, so there's stuff that you'd expect to see in a low budget movie from the 80s, I'm pretty sure I saw that a big scary monster from the movie is actually on a cart being rolled, and the laser-ish effects from the box haven't aged well either. The performances and dialogues are apt for a movie like this, but the most impressive thing about it is indeed the vision. There's all kinds of gross, twisted imagery, brilliant design, brilliant practical make-up and brilliant practical special effects throughout this film. It succeeds in what it set out to do that way. The atmosphere is great, the music is great, and it did make me squirm and uncomfortable through a lot of imaginative ways. Genuine vision and a twisted imagination from Clive Barker is on full display here. Making gross stuff be convincingly gross is indeed mastery.

Name: Hellraiser
Review:
On watching the original and this version back to back, the first thing I noticed is that this looks and feels like a modern Hollywood horror movie than the low budget indie movie original. This is definitely a bigger production, and while at first I thought a glossier version would undermine what made the original so grossly engaging, I was wrong.

This version reimagines the lore, expands upon it and it's basically a different kind of movie than the original. Like the original, this movie also relies heavily on practical effects, makeup and gore, which was the right way to go. The CGI is used to enhance the practical stuff and to do stuff that are impossible to do practically. Everything blends in perfectly, I couldn't tell apart the CG effects and practical effects, so the team has done a great job there. From the second act onwards it was a gory, gross and satisfying horror movie. The atmosphere and the kind of scares are different from what the original did, but it also stays true to the general idea of that version, of selfish humans playing with things they don't understand.

Jamie Clayton is effectively brings in the gentle and cold creepiness as The Priest AKA Pinhead and puts her own unique spin on it, a lot different from what Doug Bradley was doing in the original.

Name: The Color of Money
Review: Martin Scorsese being able to use a pool table to visually convey a character's emotions is why he's Martin Scorsese. While one master is at work behind the camera, there's another master, Paul Newman, carrying the movie giving so much depth and life to a character he had played 25 years before. The Color of Money definitely has more style than its predecessor The Hustler. Some of the pool games are even shot like full-on action sequences, there are dramatic camera moves, fast cuts and really cool use of music. Tom Cruise is really cool as the arrogant and talented Vincent, but I couldn't help but constantly be at awe at how brilliant Paul Newman is as Fast Eddie in this movie. While The Hustler was a slower character study, this is a more stylish and kinetic film, that still manages to dive deep into Fast Eddie.

Name: The Kid Detective
Review: Funny, dark, sad, deep, suspenseful and it left a lasting impression.

Name: Halloween Ends
Review:
Halloween (2018) was a pretty good revival and updation, it was faithful to the atmosphere of the original movie while being extra gory and "modern". I still love that "oner" sequence where Michael is going through a neighborhood just randomly killing people, it showed Laurie being a badass and had a satisfying showdown at the end too. 

Then came Halloween Kills, which was also marketed as having Jamie Lee as the lead, but as it turned out, Laurie is in a hospital for the most of the movie and she's just a glorified background character in it. It still had a constant momentum going on with Michael on a killing spree, a big body count and some cool kills. Eventhough it gets a bit silly at times especially towards the end and was in no way as great as its predecessor, it didn't make me feel half as disappointed as Halloween Ends did.

Halloween Kills lied to us by having Laurie all over the marketing and selling it as her movie, which it was not. Halloween Ends lies to us by having Laurie and Michael in the marketing and turning out to be neither of their movie. Well, Laurie at least gets to do more stuff here than she did in Halloween Kills, Michael on the other hand is barely in this movie. It's not even the Jaws treatment of "less is more", he's pretty irrelevant for most of this movie. It instead focuses on a new character called Corey, that too in a confusing way. It's Corey's movie for the most part, until towards the very end when it abruptly decides to become a Laurie - Michael movie, and then....it...just................ends.

There's so much stuff here that made me face-palm. There's the romance arc that made no sense, There's Alysson being so completely oblivious to the things happening around her and failing to notice obvious humongous red flags, there's Haddonfield residents being so badly written that it's so obvious that they're being set up to get murdered. Then there's the other set of silly writing regarding people being "evil" and some nonsensical stuff regarding Corey. At least Halloween Kills had the constant momentum, action and kills to make us forget about the bad writing, but here it's so apparent.

Jamie Lee definitely deserved a better conclusion to this saga than a Corey movie that becomes her movie only towards the final few minutes. Even though Jamie Lee is dependably great here, both Laurie and Alysson seem like mere shadows of themselves from the 2018 movie. Marketed as an "epic conclusion", this barely feels like it. It feels so much smaller and disconnected compared to the 2018 movie. Even the final showdown felt more thrilling there than here. Here it just seemed like they're just having it for the sake of it.

The music was cool, the music and the gore special effects are something that remained constantly great towards all 3 of these movies.
